pages.text: Today I am going on an airplane.
We pack a bag with my things.
At the airport there are many people. I stay close to my grown-up.
We wait at the gate. I can play quietly or look out of the window.
On the plane I sit in my seat and wear a seat belt.
The plane can be noisy. I can wear my headphones.
When we land, we get off the plane. I did it!
I am going to a new school.
I take my backpack with my things inside.
My new teacher says hello. She is happy to see me.
There are new children in my class. They are new to me too.
It can feel strange at first. That is okay.
Each day it feels a little more like my school.
Sometimes my school has a fire drill.
A loud bell rings. The bell is loud so everyone can hear it.
I can cover my ears if the bell is too loud.
We walk outside in a line with our teacher.
We wait outside until it is time to go back.
A fire drill is practice. It helps us stay safe.
Today I am going to the clinic for a vaccine.
A vaccine helps my body stay healthy.
The nurse cleans a small spot on my arm. It feels cold.
I might feel a quick pinch. I can squeeze my grown-up's hand.
I can look away and take a slow breath.
Then a small plaster goes on my arm.
All done! It was quick.
Today guests are coming to our home.
The doorbell may ring and people will come in.
I can say hello, or wave. Both are okay.
There will be talking and maybe tea and food.
If it gets too loud, I can go to my quiet place.
Later the guests say goodbye and go home.
Eid is a special day.
We wear new clothes.
Many family members come together. It can be busy and loud.
People may hug me or give me Eidi. I can say thank you.
There is special food and sweets.
If I need a break, I can tell my grown-up and rest in a quiet room.
Eid is a happy day for our family.
Sometimes the electricity goes off.
The lights and the fan stop. It may get dark or warm.
My grown-up can turn on a torch or a lamp.
I can stay close to my grown-up.
We can wait together and talk or sing.
The electricity comes back on. The lights work again.
We are going on a long car trip.
I sit in my seat and wear my seat belt.
The trip takes a long time. I can look at the map to see where we are.
I can bring a toy, a book or my headphones.
We stop for a break, food and the toilet.
Then we get back in the car until we arrive.
A new baby is coming to our family.
Babies sleep a lot and they cry when they need something.
Crying can be loud. I can wear headphones or go to a quiet place.
My grown-ups are busy with the baby, but they still love me.
I can help, like bringing a bottle.
I am a big brother or a big sister now.
Sometimes there is a storm.
Thunder makes a loud boom. I am safe inside.
I can cover my ears or wear headphones.
I can sit with my grown-up and hug my soft toy.
I can count slowly until the storm passes.
The storm ends and the sky is quiet again.
We are going to a wedding.
There will be many people, bright lights and music.
It can be loud. I can wear my headphones.
We will eat food. Sometimes we wait a long time for dinner.
If I feel tired or it is too much, I can tell my grown-up.
We can go outside to a quieter place for a break.
Later we go home and rest.
I like playing games.
Sometimes I win and sometimes someone else wins.
If I don't win, I might feel sad or cross. That is okay.
I can take a slow breath.
I can say "good game".
We can play again another time. Playing is fun.
